stages.name: Microfinance
stages.title: Microfinance
stages.sub: Explain microfinance as a market-orientated development strategy, and weigh its advantages and disadvantages.

steps.q: A woman in a rural village wants a small loan to buy a sewing machine, but a normal bank asks for a house or land to be put up as security before it will lend anything. She owns neither. Can she get the loan?
steps.right: No, the bank will refuse her
steps.wrong: Yes, the bank will lend anyway
steps.hint: Banks usually want something valuable held against the loan in case it is not repaid.

steps.q: Suppose a small organisation instead offers her a tiny loan with no collateral needed, judging her on her business idea rather than her assets. Does this open up a way to borrow that she did not have before?
steps.right: Yes, it gives her a new route to borrow
steps.wrong: No, she is still unable to borrow
steps.hint: She had no collateral for a bank and no safe option with the money-lender. What has changed now?

steps.q: She uses the loan to buy the sewing machine, starts selling clothes, and earns a steady income for the first time. What has this done for her and her household?
steps.right: Raised her income and reduced poverty
steps.hint: She now has a working machine and paying customers where before she had neither.

steps.right: No, it is often costly and hard to scale up
steps.wrong: Yes, it is simple to scale up profitably
